title: Check: ServiceAccounts
description: Five questions on identity for workloads.

questions.prompt: A Pod that names no serviceAccountName uses what?
questions.explanation: Every namespace gets a `default` ServiceAccount, and by default it has almost no permissions.

questions.prompt: How does a modern Kubernetes deliver a ServiceAccount token to a Pod?

options.text: As a long-lived Secret mounted automatically
As a short-lived, audience-scoped token via a projected volume
As an environment variable set by the scheduler

questions.explanation: TokenRequest-based projected tokens expire and are rotated. The old permanent Secret-based tokens are no longer created automatically.

questions.prompt: How do you stop a token being mounted into a Pod that does not need one?

options.text: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the Pod or the ServiceAccount

questions.explanation: Least privilege: a workload that never calls the API should not carry a credential for it.

questions.prompt: Where is the token mounted inside the container?
questions.explanation: Alongside ca.crt and the namespace file - everything a client library needs to talk to the API server.

questions.prompt: Write the command that creates a ServiceAccount named builder.
questions.explanation: Then bind it to a Role with `kubectl create rolebinding ... --serviceaccount=<ns>:builder`.
